# The moves (generated by tools/moves.mjs from film/src/moves/*/move.ts: do not edit)

Every move a beat file can name, by its `use`: `moves` goes on a beat as `"moves": [{ "move": "<name>", "at": <cue>, "until": <cue>, ...inputs }]`;
`cut` on the first beat of a new shot as `"cut": { "move": "<name>", ...inputs }`; `stage` as the file's `"stage"` or a scene's (`"light"`, `"dark"`, or `{ "move": "<name>", "tone": "light" | "dark", ...inputs }`; `references/stages.md`); an engine key is
written as `references/build.md` shows. Inputs that are names must be in `nodes`; cues are words of the beat's line; authored text is read by the sweep.
To see one: `node "<skill dir>/scripts/helper.mjs" moves <name> look`. A one-off (a tutorial's own film/moves/<name>/) is not listed here: its own `about` describes it.

## On a beat (`moves`)

### cards

Two to six labelled cards assemble on the stage in a row, a column or a grid, with hairlines drawn between the ones you connect: a thing, its parts, how they relate.

- use: `moves`; takes: about 2.4 s for all to land after `at`; they stay to `until`, then clear in 0.4 s
- reads: nothing of the screen; authored text: items[].label

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `items` | [{ label (authored, two to four words), lines (greek lines inside, 0 to 4) }] |
| `layout` | row (default) \| column \| grid |
| `connect` | pairs of item indexes (from 0) to join with a hairline, optional |
| `arrive` | build (default: outline, fill, contents) \| fold (each unfolds on a hinge) \| slide (each slides to its slot) |
| `each` | a cue word per item: it starts to arrive on it (default: spread over 1.2 s from `at`) |
| `at` | the cue the first arrives on (default: the line start) |
| `until` | the cue they clear on (default: the line end) |

```json
{"line":2,"moves":[{"move":"cards","at":"three","items":[{"label":"Your account","lines":3},{"label":"Its keys","lines":2},{"label":"The sandbox","lines":2}],"connect":[[0,1],[1,2]]}]}
```

### carry

A small capsule with one word sets beside an element and travels on one curve to an element of the next shot, in flight as the page changes, and rests beside that one: the thing you took here goes there.

- use: `moves`; takes: 2.2 s. It goes on the last beat before the cut: it leaves 0.2 s after it sets and lands 1.2 s later, so the cut should come within a second of `at` (a page change follows its click by 0.3 s); it rests where it landed until `until`
- reads: the named element, two screens; authored text: text

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `text` | one or two words for what is carried (authored): a name for it, never the value itself |
| `from` | a name in `nodes`: the element it sets beside (above it when the frame has room, else below; never over it), on this beat's shot (optional: top centre of the frame) |
| `to` | a name in `nodes`: the element it comes to rest beside, the same way, on the NEXT shot (optional: top centre of the frame) |
| `at` | the cue it sets on: the click that changes the page, or a word in the last half second of the line (default: the line start) |
| `until` | the cue it clears on (default: 2.2 s after it set, or the line end) |

```json
{"line":3,"moves":[{"move":"carry","text":"API key","from":"copyButton","to":"keyBox","at":"copy"}]}
```

### chip-row

A hero tile moves left from the middle of the stage and a row of small tiles appears to its right, left to right, each on its cue: these are the options.

- use: `moves`; takes: 10 frames for the hero to move, then the items; all stay to `until` and clear in 0.4 s. On a scene: it names no element and stands in the middle of the stage
- reads: nothing of the screen; authored text: hero, items

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `hero` | the hero tile's label (authored, two to four words, 40 letters at most) |
| `items` | two to five labels (authored, 16 letters at most) |
| `each` | a cue word per item (default: 4 frames apart once the hero has moved) |
| `at` | the cue the hero moves on (default: the line start; it stands in the middle from the line start until then) |
| `until` | the cue all clear on (default: the line end) |

```json
{"line":5,"scene":{},"moves":[{"move":"chip-row","hero":"Webhook events","items":["Created","Updated","Deleted"]}]}
```

### counter

A large number rolls like an odometer to a count the line says, with a plain label under it: how many of something.

- use: `moves`; takes: 1.6 s to roll and settle; 0.3 s to clear
- reads: nothing of the screen; authored text: label

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `to` | the count it lands on: a whole number the narration says (the sweep reads it as authored text) |
| `from` | the count it starts from (default 0) |
| `label` | what is counted, two to four words (authored, optional) |
| `at` | the cue the roll starts on (default: the line start) |
| `until` | the cue it clears on (default: the line end) |

```json
{"line":3,"moves":[{"move":"counter","to":77,"label":"programs","at":"seventy"}]}
```

### depth-lift

Two to four elements of the screen lift apart in depth, parallel to the page, each on its own ground with its own shadow, hold with a slow parallax and close again: what this screen is made of.

- use: `moves`; takes: 2 s at least: 0.7 s apart and 0.7 s to close, and what is between is the time to see them. The camera holds meanwhile. Each element is one more screen rebuilt per frame while they are up
- reads: the named element; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `nodes` | two to four names in `nodes`, the farthest first (a card, then a field in it, then its button): each stands a step nearer than the one before it |
| `at` | the cue they lift apart on (default: the line start) |
| `until` | the cue by which they are back in the page (default: the line end, or 2 s after they lifted) |

```json
{"line":4,"moves":[{"move":"depth-lift","nodes":["dialog","keyField","done"],"at":"made"}]}
```

### feature-list

Short nouns appear line by line beside a window held to one side (frame.side), each on its cue, a check mark before each when asked: the recap beside the thing.

- use: `moves`; takes: 0.4 s an item; they stay to `until` and clear together in 0.4 s. It names no element: it stands at a fixed place in the column a side framing leaves free, so the beat's framing has `side`
- reads: nothing of the screen; authored text: items

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `items` | two to six short nouns (authored, 28 letters at most) |
| `each` | a cue word per item (default: one every 0.5 s) |
| `checks` | true: a check mark in the accent before each |
| `side` | left (default) \| right: the side the WINDOW is framed to; the list stands on the other |
| `at` | the cue the first sets on (default: the line start) |
| `until` | the cue all clear on (default: the line end) |

```json
{"line":7,"frame":{"whole":true,"side":"left"},"moves":[{"move":"feature-list","items":["Name","Email","Username"],"each":["name","email","username"],"checks":true}]}
```

### icon-lift

One element grows to one and a half times its size in its place over ten frames while what is around it dims a fifth, holds, and comes back: the one focus move that is not a cut. No blur, no travel.

- use: `moves`; takes: 1.2 s at least: 10 frames up and 10 down. What dims is the element's surroundings, an oval round it that falls away to nothing, not the whole frame: the same on a whole screen, in a window and on a bare shot. One more screen rebuilt per frame while it is up
- reads: the named element; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `target` | a name in `nodes`: the element that grows (an icon, a button, a field) |
| `at` | the cue it grows on (default: the line start) |
| `until` | the cue by which it is back (default: the line end, or 1.2 s after) |

```json
{"line":4,"moves":[{"move":"icon-lift","target":"viewKey","at":"view"}]}
```

### impact-lines

Six to eight short strokes burst outward from the edge of an element (or from the middle of the frame) and are gone in a third of a second: the moment something lands.

- use: `moves`; takes: 0.35 s
- reads: the named element; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `target` | a name in `nodes`: the element they burst from (optional: without it, the middle of the frame) |
| `at` | the cue they burst on (default: the line start) |

```json
{"line":2,"moves":[{"move":"impact-lines","target":"save","at":"saved"}]}
```

### keycaps

The keys of a shortcut as plain keycaps in a row near the frame's bottom, set on the cue and gone 1.2 s later: or press these keys.

- use: `moves`; takes: 1.5 s: 0.2 s to set, 1.2 s held, 0.25 s to leave
- reads: nothing of the screen; authored text: caps

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `caps` | one to four key names (authored): Ctrl, Shift, K, Enter, each 6 letters at most |
| `at` | the cue they set on (default: the line start) |
| `until` | the cue they leave on (default: 1.2 s after they set, or the line end) |

```json
{"line":3,"moves":[{"move":"keycaps","caps":["Ctrl","K"],"at":"press"}]}
```

### label-beside

A short label beside a window held to one side (frame.side) whose words change on each cue with the word swap's motion: a feature label beside the device, the step counter without a step counter.

- use: `moves`; takes: 0.4 s to set, 0.21 s a swap; stays to `until`. It names no element: it stands at a fixed place in the column a side framing leaves free, level with the middle of the frame, so the beat's framing has `side`
- reads: nothing of the screen; authored text: words

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `words` | one to six short labels, in the order they show (authored, 24 letters at most) |
| `each` | a cue word per change (one fewer than `words`; default: one every 0.9 s) |
| `side` | left (default) \| right: the side the WINDOW is framed to (the same word as the framing's `side`); the label stands on the other |
| `at` | the cue the label sets on (default: the line start) |
| `until` | the cue it clears on (default: the line end) |

```json
{"line":3,"frame":{"whole":true,"side":"left"},"moves":[{"move":"label-beside","words":["Open the menu","Choose Profile"],"each":["profile"]}]}
```

### labels

Plain labels set beside one to four elements of the screen, each on its cue word, and clear together: these fields, named in place.

- use: `moves`; takes: 0.3 s a label, 0.3 s to clear; they stay to `until`. Beside a screen framed close a label may stand over a neighbour (a move knows no layout): frame the group
- reads: the named element; authored text: items[].text

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `items` | [{ target: a name in `nodes`, text: its label (authored, 30 letters at most) }], one to four |
| `each` | a cue word per item: its label sets on it (default: spread over 1.2 s from `at`) |
| `at` | the cue the first label sets on (default: the line start) |
| `until` | the cue all clear on (default: the line end) |

```json
{"line":2,"moves":[{"move":"labels","items":[{"target":"firstName","text":"Your name"},{"target":"username","text":"Your sign-in name"}],"each":["name","username"]}]}
```

### lift-out

One element rises off the page to the middle of the frame and grows while the screen draws back and softens under it, then is set down again: the one thing this line is about, large enough to read.

- use: `moves`; takes: 1.5 s at least: 0.6 s up and 0.6 s down, and what is between is the time to read it. The camera holds meanwhile (keep the framing over its beat), and twice in a row is a second lift, not a longer one. Each lift is one more screen rebuilt per frame while it is up
- reads: the named element; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `node` | a name in `nodes`: the element that is lifted out (a field, a row, a card, a dialog) |
| `strength` | 1 \| 2 (default) \| 3: how large it stands, 0.6, 0.72 or 0.85 of the frame's width (less when it is tall) |
| `at` | the cue it rises on (default: the line start) |
| `until` | the cue by which it is back in its place (default: the line end, or 1.5 s after it rose) |

```json
{"line":3,"moves":[{"move":"lift-out","node":"keyField","at":"key"}]}
```

### mark-time

A short plain label on the stage, low and centred, from one cue to another: "Step 2", "Before", a name.

- use: `moves`; takes: 0.4 s to set, 0.3 s to clear
- reads: nothing of the screen; authored text: text

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `text` | two to four words (authored) |
| `at` | the cue it sets on (default: the line start) |
| `until` | the cue it clears on (default: the line end) |

```json
{"line":1,"moves":[{"move":"mark-time","text":"Step 2","at":"open","until":"profile"}]}
```

### pin

A small pin drops onto an element's top right corner and a card with a few plain words slides out beside it, clear of the element: a remark on one thing.

- use: `moves`; takes: 1.4 s at least: the pin drops in 0.35 s, the card is out 0.6 s after the cue; both stay to `until` and leave in 0.3 s
- reads: the named element; authored text: text

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `target` | a name in `nodes`: the element the pin is put on |
| `text` | the remark (authored): a few plain words, 36 letters at most |
| `at` | the cue the pin drops on (default: the line start) |
| `until` | the cue both leave on (default: the line end, or 1.4 s after the drop) |

```json
{"line":4,"moves":[{"move":"pin","target":"keyField","text":"Shown once only","at":"key"}]}
```

### scan

A light passes once, left to right, over an element or the whole frame while the rest dims a little: something is being read or checked.

- use: `moves`; takes: 1.4 s (up to 2.4 s when the line is longer)
- reads: the named element; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `target` | a name in `nodes`: the element it passes over (optional: without it, the whole frame) |
| `kind` | line (default: a soft upright band) \| cone (a soft round window) |
| `at` | the cue the pass starts on (default: the line start) |
| `until` | the cue it has crossed by (default: 1.4 s later, or the line end; never slower than 2.4 s) |

```json
{"line":5,"moves":[{"move":"scan","target":"report","at":"checks"}]}
```

### sheet-stack

Two to thirteen sheets riffle in from below into one stack, each with a numbered tab at its top edge: rounds, versions, pages, a pile of the same kind of thing.

- use: `moves`; takes: 1.8 s at least: the sheets come over 1.2 s, the last has set 0.5 s later; the stack stays to `until` and clears in 0.4 s
- reads: nothing of the screen; authored text: labels[]

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `count` | how many sheets, 2 to 13 (a count the film shows) |
| `labels` | optional: a short word per tab in place of its number (authored), the back sheet first; the more sheets, the shorter they must be |
| `at` | the cue the first sheet comes on (default: the line start) |
| `until` | the cue the stack clears on (default: the line end, or 1.8 s after it started) |

```json
{"line":2,"moves":[{"move":"sheet-stack","count":5,"at":"rounds"}]}
```

### split

The same element from two screens side by side, before on the left and after on the right, each on its own ground, the after pane settling last: see what changed.

- use: `moves`; takes: 2 s at least: the panes rise over 0.5 s, the after 0.25 s later; both stay to `until` and set down in 0.4 s. Each is captioned, Before and After. Two more screens rebuilt per frame while they are up
- reads: the named element, two screens; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `before` | a name in `nodes`: the element on the screen before this shot's |
| `after` | a name in `nodes`: the same element on this shot's screen |
| `at` | the cue the panes rise on (default: the line start) |
| `until` | the cue they set down by (default: the line end, or 2 s after they rose) |

```json
{"line":4,"moves":[{"move":"split","before":"statusBefore","after":"statusAfter","at":"changed"}]}
```

### spotlight

The frame dims around a soft-edged window on one element for a beat, then lifts: only this part.

- use: `moves`; takes: 1.2 s at least: 0.3 s in, 0.3 s out. One spotlight at a time
- reads: the named element; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `target` | a name in `nodes`: the element kept lit |
| `tight` | true: the lit window is the element's box exactly, with a 4 px feather (a table row lit and nothing past it; default: grown a tenth each way, a 12 px feather) |
| `at` | the cue the dim comes on (default: the line start) |
| `until` | the cue it lifts by (default: the line end, or 1.2 s after) |

```json
{"line":5,"moves":[{"move":"spotlight","target":"keyField","at":"key"}]}
```

### step-counter

A quiet "2 of 5" at the frame's top right corner over the line that starts a step: where you are in a procedure of five steps or more. Once per step, opt in per film; plain type, no box.

- use: `moves`; takes: 0.3 s to set; stays to `until` (the line end); 0.3 s to clear
- reads: nothing of the screen; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `step` | which step this is (a number, from 1) |
| `of` | how many steps there are (2 to 12) |
| `at` | the cue it sets on (default: the line start) |
| `until` | the cue it clears on (default: the line end) |

```json
{"line":2,"moves":[{"move":"step-counter","step":2,"of":5}]}
```

### type-beat

Two to four words alone on the stage in the title's type, rising into place and clearing upward: a breath between two parts of a long film.

- use: `moves`; takes: 1.6 s at least: 0.8 s to rise, 0.4 s to clear. On a scene (`scene: {}`): the cursor is off meanwhile
- reads: nothing of the screen; authored text: text

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `text` | two to four words (authored); never a slogan or a status word |
| `at` | the cue it rises on (default: the line start) |
| `until` | the cue it has cleared by (default: the line end, or 1.6 s after) |

```json
{"line":6,"scene":{},"moves":[{"move":"type-beat","text":"Now the webhook"}]}
```

### word-swap

A short phrase in large type whose last word swaps for the next on each cue: a status that changes, a name that becomes another.

- use: `moves`; takes: 0.4 s to set, 0.21 s a swap, 0.3 s to clear
- reads: nothing of the screen; authored text: before, words

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `before` | the words that stay, before the one that swaps (authored, optional) |
| `words` | two to five words or short phrases, in the order they show (authored) |
| `each` | a cue word per swap (one fewer than `words`): the next word comes on it (default: one swap every 0.9 s) |
| `at` | the cue the phrase sets on (default: the line start) |
| `until` | the cue it clears on (default: the line end) |

```json
{"line":4,"moves":[{"move":"word-swap","before":"Status","words":["In review","Approved"],"at":"status","each":["approved"]}]}
```

## Between shots (`cut`)

### covered-swap

The window grows until it covers the frame, becomes the new shot while nothing else can be seen, and settles back: a page change, or a change of stage, hidden under the window itself.

- use: `cut`; takes: 0.9 s; both shots are framed on their whole window (a window that stands smaller than 0.75 of the frame does not cover it)
- reads: two screens; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|

```json
{"line":2,"screen":1,"cut":{"move":"covered-swap"}}
```

### gradient-cross

The camera pans down (or across) one long gradient from the light stage to the dark, or back; the shot before leans back and leaves ahead of it, and the new shot is where the camera comes to rest: a change of world.

- use: `cut`; takes: 3.1 s: the shot before has left within two seconds, the new one arrives over the last one. Into or out of a scene, that side is the bare stage
- reads: two screens; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `to` | light \| dark: the stage it arrives on. It must be the stage of the shot it leads into (a scene's own `stage`, or the film's when it leads out of a scene). For a named stage it is that stage's `tone`: the stage shows through the gradient's clear ends |
| `axis` | v (default): the camera pans down \| h: it pans to the right |

```json
{"line":3,"scene":{"stage":"dark"},"cut":{"move":"gradient-cross","to":"dark"}}
```

### line-pass

A ribbon runs in under the shot before and on ahead; the camera rides after it in one move to the new shot, and the ribbon has left by the time it settles: time passing, or a step on to what comes next.

- use: `cut`; takes: 3.3 s, the longest way into a shot but one: leave it a line of its own, or the end of one. Nothing is blurred, so both shots are best framed on their whole window
- reads: two screens; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `variant` | below (default): the new shot stands lower, and the camera drops onto it as the ribbon goes by above \| side: the camera stays level and the ribbon turns up and away just short of the new shot |

```json
{"line":2,"screen":1,"cut":{"move":"line-pass","variant":"below"}}
```

### match-cut

One object that is on both shots carries the cut: the shot before travels until the object is where, and as large as, it is on the new shot, and the cut lands as it arrives. Only for the same thing on both sides.

- use: `cut`; takes: 1.6 s: it gathers speed slowly, so most of the travel is in the half second before the cut, which lands 1.16 s in
- reads: the named element, two screens; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `hero` | two names in `nodes`: the object on the shot before, and the same object on the new shot |

```json
{"line":4,"screen":2,"cut":{"move":"match-cut","hero":["row","page"]}}
```

### pull-back

A hard cut lands close on one element of the new shot, twice the size the shot frames it, and pulls back to the shot's framing in one move, fast off the mark and settling long: from a detail to its place.

- use: `cut`; takes: 0.8 s; the shot before is gone at once and the new page is there whole (nothing sets in). A cursor on the new shot is enlarged with it. The shot's own slow push follows: `hold` on its first framing for a dead stop
- reads: the named element, two screens; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `from` | a name in `nodes`: the element on the NEW shot's screen the cut lands on (one the page shows at the cut: not something a later click opens) |

```json
{"line":3,"screen":1,"cut":{"move":"pull-back","from":"keyField"}}
```

### stage-push

The shot before slides off one side, shrinking and softening, while the new one follows it in on the same move: a step sideways to another place of the same standing.

- use: `cut`; takes: 0.8 s
- reads: two screens; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `direction` | left (default) \| right \| up \| down: the way the outgoing shot leaves; the new one comes in after it |

```json
{"line":2,"screen":1,"cut":{"move":"stage-push","direction":"left"}}
```

### zoom-through

The picture travels into the element that was clicked until it fills the frame, and the new shot comes out of it and settles: going into the thing you chose.

- use: `cut`; takes: 1 s; cue the click a second before the line that follows, or the shot before holds meanwhile
- reads: the named element, two screens; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `through` | a name in `nodes`: the element on the shot before that the picture travels into (the one the cursor clicked) |

```json
{"line":3,"screen":1,"cut":{"move":"zoom-through","through":"profileItem"}}
```

## Stages (`stage`)

### light

The house light stage: a pale field, two slow orbs, a fixed dither.

- use: `stage`; takes: the film, or a scene
- reads: nothing of the screen; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `stage` | "light" (the default: a film that names no stage, under a brand with none of its own, is on it). A named stage is written { "move": "<stage>", "tone": ..., ...inputs } in the same place |

```json
{"stage":"light"}
```

### dark

The dark stage: a deep field with one slow glow; cards glow instead of casting shadow. A recorded window keeps its own light shadow on it.

- use: `stage`; takes: the film, or a scene
- reads: nothing of the screen; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `stage` | "dark", as the file's `stage` or a scene's |

```json
{"stage":"dark"}
```

### environment

A wall and a floor: a wall lit from one side, a floor plane at 0.62 of the frame's height with a soft band where they meet; windows keep their shadow. A sense of place, with no reflection of the content.

- use: `stage`; takes: the film, or a scene. It does not move
- reads: nothing of the screen; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `light` | left (default) \| right \| top: the side the light is on |
| `floor` | false: the wall alone (default: the floor is there) |
| `tone` | light (default) \| dark: a pale room or a dark one, and which ink and cards go in it |

```json
{"stage":{"move":"environment","light":"left"}}
```

### field

A solid or two-colour gradient ground with the kit's dither, its angle drifting a little: a brand's own colour behind the film.

- use: `stage`; takes: the film, or a scene
- reads: the brand; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `colour` | one CSS colour: a solid field; or |
| `from` | the gradient's first colour, and |
| `to` | its second (the word accent, in any of the three, is the brand's accent) |
| `angle` | degrees, 0 to 359 (default 160) |
| `tone` | light (default) \| dark: which ink and cards go on it. Say dark for a deep colour |

```json
{"stage":{"move":"field","from":"accent","to":"#102040","tone":"dark"}}
```

### footage

A clip the user supplied playing behind the film, muted, covering the frame under a scrim of the stage's own colour so type and cards read on it.

- use: `stage`; takes: the film, or a scene. The clip runs on the film's clock (a scene sees it where the film has got to), is never trimmed and never heard. Each frame of it is one more picture to decode: a render is slower
- reads: a supplied file; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `file` | a plain file name (mp4, webm) in the tutorial's film/media/, or brand/<file name> for a clip in the brand's folder |
| `loop` | the clip's length in seconds: it plays again from its start each time it ends (without it a clip shorter than the film holds its last frame) |
| `scrim` | 0 to 1: how much of the stage's colour lies over the clip (default 0.6) |
| `tone` | light (default) \| dark: the scrim's colour, and which ink and cards go on it |

```json
{"stage":{"move":"footage","file":"brand/loop.mp4","loop":6,"tone":"dark"}}
```

### image

A picture the user supplied as the ground, covering the frame under a scrim of the stage's own colour (pale on light, deep on dark) so type and cards read on it.

- use: `stage`; takes: the film, or a scene. It does not move. A recorded window stands on it with its own ground and shadow; a `bare` shot's elements stand on it on the page's own colour
- reads: a supplied file; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `file` | a plain file name (png, jpg, jpeg, webp) in the tutorial's film/media/, or brand/<file name> for a picture in the brand's folder |
| `scrim` | 0 to 1: how much of the stage's colour lies over the picture (default 0.6; 0: the picture as it is, for a film with no type on the stage) |
| `fit` | cover (default) \| contain |
| `tone` | light (default) \| dark: the scrim's colour, and which ink and cards go on it |

```json
{"stage":{"move":"image","file":"texture.png","tone":"dark"}}
```

## The engine's own (by their keys)

### browser-bar

A neutral browser tab strip, toolbar and bookmarks row that grows out of the top of the window for a step taken in the browser itself, then goes back in.

- use: `bar`; takes: grows in about 0.55 s and is whole 0.3 s before the click on its hero; goes back in over 0.55 s once its line has been said, or (leaves: with-camera) is carried out by the next camera move
- reads: nothing of the screen; authored text: title, host, bookmarks[].label

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `title` | the tab's title (authored) |
| `host` | the address shown (a made-up one, authored) |
| `bookmarks` | label + icon name, in order (labels authored) |
| `hero` | the bookmark the cursor presses (target "bar:hero") |
| `from` | a cue word to start growing on, optional |
| `arrives` | how what the hero opens comes: down (from under the bar, the default) \| right (a short slide in from the window's right edge, fading up) \| appear (set in place whole) |
| `leaves` | with-camera: it does not go back in; the shot's next framing starts once what the hero opened has arrived and carries the bar out of the frame's top (optional; that framing must leave the window's top out of the frame) |

```json
{"line":6,"bar":{"title":"Webhooks","host":"app.example.com","hero":"Autofill","bookmarks":[{"label":"Inbox","icon":"inbox"},{"label":"Autofill","icon":"bookmark"}]},"then":[{"cursor":"click","target":"bar:hero","cue":"bookmarklet"}]}
```

### title

The title alone on the stage, rising into place; it clears upward 1.3 s before the first line. The open of a film that names no other.

- use: `title`; takes: the 3.6 s before line 0
- reads: nothing of the screen; authored text: title

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `title` | the file's `title` (authored) |

```json
{"title":"Find your user API key"}
```

### title-makes-room

The first screen is on the stage from the first frame, still and centred at 0.62 of its size for 0.6 s, then slides to a third of the frame over 8 frames while the title fades in beside it; a second before the first line the title goes, the window returns to centre at its size, and the camera begins.

- use: `open`; takes: the time before line 0 (3.6 s as the narration is timed: the title is up for about 1.5 s of it). The first shot is its whole screen; the camera's first move and the cursor wait until the window is back (0.3 s before the line)
- reads: the clean screen; authored text: title

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `open` | the file's `open`: { "move": "title-makes-room" } |

```json
{"open":{"move":"title-makes-room"}}
```

### cut-to-screen

No title: the film opens on the first screen already placed, content on; the first line begins.

- use: `open`; takes: nothing of its own: the screen holds for the time before line 0
- reads: the clean screen; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `open` | the file's `open`: { "move": "cut-to-screen" } |

```json
{"open":{"move":"cut-to-screen"}}
```

### window

The recorded screen as a window on the stage: it settles in as the title clears and gives way before the end card.

- use: `screen`; takes: 0.75 s to settle; 0.5 s to leave
- reads: the clean screen; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `screen` | a screen number on the first beat of a shot |
| `window` | optional: names in `nodes`; the shot shows those elements alone |

```json
{"line":0,"screen":2}
```

### bare-ui

The window's elements alone on the stage with no frame and no shadow, each on the page's own colour: the interface without its device.

- use: `screen`; takes: the shot, or until a `frame-back`
- reads: the named elements of the clean screen; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `window` | names in `nodes`: the elements shown |
| `bare` | true, beside `window` on the first beat of the shot |

```json
{"line":1,"screen":3,"window":"card","bare":true}
```

### framing

Where the camera is by this beat: the whole screen, a target with its row, group or corner, or several targets held together. By default one continuous camera per screen, every hold a slow push; the two exceptions are `cut` (the camera cuts to the framing) and `hold` (the camera does not move for the shot).

- use: `frame`; takes: 1.2 s plus 0.85 s per doubling of the scale
- reads: measured boxes, clean/layout.json; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `whole` | true |
| `target` | a name |
| `with` | self \| row \| group \| corner |
| `targets` | names |
| `back` | true: may pull back |
| `side` | left \| right: what is framed stands to that side of the stage at half the frame's width at most, the other side free for type (label-beside, feature-list); a shot's first framing, or pulled back or cut to |
| `cut` | true: the camera cuts to this framing (a hard cut, no travel; wider or tighter) |
| `hold` | true (on a shot's first framing): the camera does not drift at all for this shot: all change is inside the screen |

```json
{"line":1,"frame":{"target":"userMenu","with":"corner"}}
```

### framing-cut

A hard cut from one framing of the screen to another, a larger crop of the part that matters or back to the whole: no animated zoom. The cursor stays on what it points at.

- use: `frame`; takes: one frame, a tenth of a second before the beat's cue or action (where a travelling camera would arrive)
- reads: measured boxes; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `cut` | true, on any framing after a shot's first |

```json
{"line":2,"frame":{"target":"card","cut":true}}
```

### device-hold

The window does not move for the whole shot: no drift, no settling in after the cut. All change is inside the screen.

- use: `frame`; takes: the shot
- reads: measured boxes; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `hold` | true, on the first framing of a shot |

```json
{"line":0,"screen":2,"frame":{"whole":true,"hold":true}}
```

### cursor

The one pointer: enters, travels on bowed paths, rests beside or clicks on a named element on its cue word (the control takes the page's own hover and press look), drags one to another place, and leaves.

- use: `cursor`; takes: 0.7 to 2.4 s per travel
- reads: measured boxes and spots; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `cursor` | enter \| click \| rest \| move \| drag \| leave |
| `target` | a name |
| `cue` | a word of the line |
| `to` | a drag: the name it is dropped on |
| `release` | a drag: the later cue word it is let go on |
| `then` | further actions in the line |

```json
{"line":3,"cursor":"click","target":"viewKey","cue":"api"}
```

### opens

A menu or dialog shut until the click on `after`, then uncovered from its top edge or set whole in place, opaque throughout.

- use: `change`; takes: 0.3 s
- reads: the hidden node of the screen; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `node` | a name |
| `after` | the name clicked |
| `unhide` | optional: true when the capture holds it display:none (a hover menu): the film displays it, so it and its items measure |

```json
{"change":{"kind":"opens","node":"menu","after":"userMenu"}}
```

### close

A menu or dialog goes the way it came: covered back to its top edge, or shrinking to 88 % as its backdrop dims out, hidden after 0.3 s; on the beat's cue, else its line start.

- use: `change`; takes: 0.3 s
- reads: the node of the screen; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `node` | a name: the node an `opens` showed (or one the capture shows open) |

```json
{"line":5,"cue":"done","change":{"kind":"close","node":"dialog"}}
```

### hover

A tip or menu that exists only under the pointer: uncovered when the cursor rests on its control, which takes the page's hover look; gone when the cursor moves on. It shows a hover the recording contains.

- use: `change`; takes: 0.3 s to come, 0.3 s to go
- reads: the node of the screen; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `node` | a name: the tip, as the capture holds it |
| `after` | a name: the control, which a `rest` or `move` on the shot goes to |

```json
{"line":7,"cursor":"rest","target":"viewKey","cue":"button","change":{"kind":"hover","node":"tip","after":"viewKey"}}
```

### page-cut

A hard cut to the next screen 0.3 s after the click that causes it (or 0.3 s before its line); the new page's parts set in place.

- use: `change`; takes: 0.45 s of assembly
- reads: two clean screens; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `kind` | "page" |

```json
{"line":2,"screen":1,"change":{"kind":"page"}}
```

### selects

A value shows selected from the click on it; with `to`, a block is selected line by line down to the cue.

- use: `change`; takes: 8 frames
- reads: the field; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `node` | a name |
| `to` | a later cue word (a block) |

```json
{"change":{"kind":"selects","node":"keyField"}}
```

### fills

A field empty until its click, then its value whole (a paste) or letter by letter (typing) to a cue; the value is the clean copy's or authored words.

- use: `change`; takes: about a second typed
- reads: the field; authored text: text

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `node` | a name |
| `typed` | true |
| `text` | authored words |
| `to` | a cue word |

```json
{"change":{"kind":"fills","node":"name","typed":true,"text":"Example Co"}}
```

### scrolls

The content of a shot moves up in one eased move to its bottom, its top, or a named element: a windowed shot's nodes in their window, or a whole screen's own page (to a named element).

- use: `change`; takes: 1.2 to 4 s
- reads: the windowed element, or the clean screen's document; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `to` | bottom \| top \| a name |

```json
{"change":{"kind":"scrolls","to":"bottom"}}
```

### becomes

The shot's screen becomes a later capture of the same page, in place, under the same camera; an element that grew is carried to its new box.

- use: `change`; takes: 0.3 s after the click; 0.5 s of growth
- reads: two clean screens; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `screen` | a screen number |
| `after` | the name clicked |
| `grows` | [name before, name after] |

```json
{"change":{"kind":"becomes","screen":23,"after":"save"}}
```

### device-comes-back

On a bare shot the window's frame and shadow fade in round the elements over 10 frames without moving them: from a detail back to the whole without a zoom.

- use: `change`; takes: 10 frames
- reads: nothing more of the screen; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `kind` | "frame-back", on a beat of a shot that is `bare`; it comes on the beat's cue, else with its line |

```json
{"line":2,"cue":"page","change":{"kind":"frame-back"}}
```

### hold-while-it-changes

Change in place: the window is held still and the screen becomes its next capture inside it. A `becomes` under a held framing.

- use: `change`; takes: 0.3 s after the click
- reads: two clean screens; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `hold` | true on the shot's first framing |
| `change` | a `becomes` |

```json
{"line":3,"frame":{"whole":true,"hold":true},"change":{"kind":"becomes","screen":5,"after":"save"}}
```

### screen-swap

The swap on one stage: the same window in the same place, its content cut to another screen; the new page is there whole, nothing sets in. A `page` change with `hold` on both shots: before and after, or past a long interaction.

- use: `change`; takes: one frame
- reads: two clean screens; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `hold` | true on the first framing of both shots |
| `change` | { "kind": "page" } |

```json
{"line":4,"screen":6,"frame":{"whole":true,"hold":true},"change":{"kind":"page"}}
```

### sequence

The page works by itself: captures play at the recorded pace, then evenly over the rest of the line, in place.

- use: `sequence`; takes: the line
- reads: many clean screens; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `from` | a screen |
| `watch` | the last watched screen |
| `then` | screens |
| `follow` | a scroll box kept at its end |

```json
{"line":12,"sequence":{"from":29,"watch":40,"then":[60,77]}}
```

### narrated-list

The screen recedes behind a blur and wash; the line's items set as large type after an icon, each on its word; all clear together.

- use: `list`; takes: the line plus 0.7 s to clear
- reads: nothing of the screen; authored text: items[].text

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `from` | a cue word |
| `items` | [{ text (authored), icon (a set name), cue }] |

```json
{"list":{"items":[{"text":"Your sign-in name","icon":"user-round","cue":"name"}]}}
```

### end-card

The brand's mark sets (or builds part by part: brand.json mark.build) and is swept once; the closing line plays over it; with no mark, the title as text. Every film ends on it; `logo-lift` and `end-glyph` are other ways into it.

- use: `end`; takes: 1.85 s (2.75 built) plus a 2.2 s hold
- reads: the brand; authored text: title

| input | what |
|---|---|

```json
{}
```

### logo-lift

The way into the end card from the recorded site's own logo: the camera pushes toward it, the window is gone over the last of the push, and the brand's mark comes up out of it and sets in its place. For a film whose brand is the site it shows.

- use: `end`; takes: 1.1 s of push, starting 0.6 s before the window would leave; the close's own times do not change. The last shot is a whole screen (no window, not a scene). A mark that is built on, or a card of text, sets in the usual way after the push
- reads: the named element, the brand; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `end` | the file's `end`: { "move": "logo-lift", "from": a name in `nodes`, the logo on the last shot's screen } |

```json
{"end":{"move":"logo-lift","from":"logo"}}
```

### end-glyph

The way into the end card from a glyph of the subject: a hard cut to one named element alone in the middle of the stage, its parts sliding a little apart and back, the brand's mark coming up out of it as the card sets while the glyph goes.

- use: `end`; takes: the cut comes 1.5 s before the window would have left (2.35 s before the closing line: the line before it should be over by then, or a note says so); the close's own times do not change. The last shot is a whole screen. The glyph stands 0.3 of the frame wide (less when tall) on the page's own colour; an element of one part does not part
- reads: the named element, the brand; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `end` | the file's `end`: { "move": "end-glyph", "glyph": a name in `nodes`, an element of the screen the film ends on } |

```json
{"end":{"move":"end-glyph","glyph":"card"}}
```

### fade

The way into the end card by a fade alone: the last shot holds exactly where it is (the camera stands still, the window neither scales nor rises) and fades out while the end card sets in; the mark builds or sets as ever. For a film that should end without more motion.

- use: `end`; takes: the camera stands still from when the window would have started to leave; the window fades over 0.8 s from then, 0.3 s of it over the end card as it sets. The close's own times do not change
- reads: nothing more of the screen; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|
| `end` | the file's `end`: { "move": "fade" } |

```json
{"end":{"move":"fade"}}
```

### chalk

Not available from the beat file yet (`chalk: []`; nothing reads it): a chalk circle drawn on in frame space (kit/ChalkMark).

- use: `chalk`; takes: 14 frames
- reads: a measured box; authored text: none

| input | what |
|---|---|

```json
{"chalk":[]}
```
